data_element: Factory calendar, shifts and plant shutdowns
description: Working days, shift pattern per department, public holidays (Italy/Trentino), planned shutdowns (August, Christmas) and Saturday overtime. These are known future covariates that shift both inflow and outflow.
typical_source_system: SAP factory calendar; HR/shift planning; MES
example_fields: date, is_workday, shifts_moulding, shifts_assembly, shutdown_flag, holiday_name
evidence: 'Can we accurately forecast non-elective bed occupancy...' found day-of-week and holiday variables improved accuracy. 'Temporal Fusion Transformers' formalises calendar features as known-future inputs.
proxy_if_missing: Build the calendar from Italian public holidays plus Coster's announced shutdowns and assume the standard shift pattern.
sap_objects: TFACS (IDENT, JAHR, MON01-MON12, WENUM workdays), TFACD (definition). Shift and work-center capacity tables (TC37A, KAKO, CRHD) unverified.

description: Date and content of every AW reconfiguration (August 2026 re-layout), cell-class counts before and after, rule changes (caps, defrag threshold, allocation reserve). It marks the structural breaks that limit usable history.
typical_source_system: Coster maintenance / IT change records
example_fields: change_date, change_type, cells_by_class_before, cells_by_class_after, rule_changed, notes
evidence: The Chalmers lead-time thesis notes that its roughly two-year history covers the post-COVID recovery phase, which adds uncertainty. 'Data quality problems in discrete event simulation...' (Bokrantz et al. 2018) lists data sources not designed for simulation among the data quality problems.
proxy_if_missing: Interview the WMS owner. Detect breaks as step changes in the per-class total cell counts in the snapshots.
sap_objects: No SAP object. Change documents (CDHDR/CDPOS) only if layout parameters are SAP-managed.
check_note: Independent check: corrected. Chalmers thesis (Sitje & Waldschock 2025) says its ~2-year post-COVID history adds uncertainty; Bokrantz et al. (2018) list data sources not designed for simulation as one of several problems, not a core one; CDHDR is the change-document header table.

description: Components and quantities per assembled valve or actuator (cups, valve bodies, springs, gaskets, packaging), with scrap allowance. Each assembly WO pulls component pallboxes out of the AW and pushes finished pallets in.
typical_source_system: SAP PP (BOM)
example_fields: parent_material, component, qty_per, uom, component_scrap_pct, valid_from
evidence: 'ISA-95 Common Object Model (OPC 10030)' assembles material definitions from other definitions and lots from sublots. Simulation input studies ('Input data management in simulation') list BOM and routing data among the core inputs.
proxy_if_missing: Use the empirical ratio of component goods issues to finished goods receipts per WO.
sap_objects: STKO (header, unverified), STPO (IDNRK, MENGE, MEINS, AUSCH), RESB (order-specific components).

data_element: Production confirmations and goods receipts from production
description: Actual produced quantities and times per order (yield, scrap, rework, actual start and finish) and the goods-receipt postings. They give plan-versus-actual for slips and quantity deviations and close the flow balance.
typical_source_system: SAP PP confirmations; SAP MM material documents; MES
example_fields: order_id, conf_ts, yield_qty, scrap_qty, rework_qty, actual_start, actual_finish, gr_doc, gr_ts
evidence: 'Modeling for Non-Exponential Production Systems Using Parts Flow Data' estimates system behaviour from part counts because machine status data are of low quality. 'Data quality problems in discrete event simulation...' lists missing minor-stoppage data.
proxy_if_missing: Use AW putaway events of finished pallets from the movement log as the actual inflow timestamps.
sap_objects: AFRU (LMNGA, XMNGA, RMNGA, ISDD/ISDZ, IEDD/IEDZ, BUDAT), AFPO.WEMNG, MATDOC (replaces MSEG/MKPF; movement-type and timestamp fields unverified).
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. leanx confirms AFRU fields (LMNGA, XMNGA, RMNGA, ISDD/ISDZ, IEDD/IEDZ, BUDAT) and AFPO.WEMNG; sapdocs says MATDOC replaces MSEG/MKPF; Sun & Zhang cite low-quality operating status data; Bokrantz lists missing minor-stoppage data.

description: Actual receipt date and time and quantity for each PO line, plus the pallet count. Together with the PO dates they give supplier slip distributions.
typical_source_system: SAP MM goods receipts; goods-in log; WMS putaway
example_fields: po, item, gr_doc, gr_ts, qty, n_pallets, supplier
evidence: 'Lead time forecasting for supplier management using machine learning' uses actual vs expected lead time from ERP PO lines. 'Supply chain data analytics for predicting supplier disruptions' predicts late orders with ~80% accuracy.
proxy_if_missing: Use EKET.WEMNG changes between daily exports, or AW putaways of purchased materials.
sap_objects: MATDOC (GR postings with PO reference; fields unverified), EKET.WEMNG, EKES (inbound delivery link). EKBE (PO history) unverified.

description: Distribution of (actual receipt date - promised date) and of quantity deviations per supplier and material group. These feed the Monte Carlo plan slips for purchased inflows.
typical_source_system: Derived from PO schedule lines + goods receipts
example_fields: supplier, material_group, n_lines, slip_days_quantiles, qty_dev_quantiles, early_share, late_share
evidence: In the Chalmers lead-time thesis, CatBoost on ERP PO lines beat supplier estimates (0.804 vs 0.343 binned accuracy), and engineered delay features mattered. In 'Supply chain data analytics for predicting supplier disruptions', engineered 'agility' features gave the best model.
proxy_if_missing: Ask planners for typical early and late days per key supplier and use a triangular distribution.
sap_objects: EKET (EINDT vs GR date), EKES (confirmed vs actual), MARC.PLIFZ (planned delivery days).

description: Scheduled versus actual start, finish and quantity for completed orders. This is the empirical slip distribution behind the '~90% of the next 10 days realised' figure, and you need it per department.
typical_source_system: SAP PP order header (scheduled vs actual dates); MES
example_fields: order_id, dept, sched_start, actual_start, sched_finish, actual_finish, planned_qty, actual_qty
evidence: 'New lot-sizing formulations for less nervous production schedules' measures nervousness as differences between successive schedules. 'An approach for increasing the level of accuracy in supply chain simulation by using patterns on input data' mines patterns in input data.
proxy_if_missing: AFKO keeps both scheduled and actual dates for each order. The last scheduled date versus actual is a lower bound on slip; plan vintages from the daily exports give the full picture going forward.
sap_objects: AFKO (GSTRS/GLTRS scheduled vs GSTRI/GLTRI actual, GETRI confirmed finish), AFPO (PSMNG vs WEMNG, DGLTP vs LTRMI).
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. leanx confirms AFKO GSTRS/GLTRS/GSTRI/GLTRI/GETRI and AFPO PSMNG/WEMNG/DGLTP/LTRMI; Kazan et al. measure nervousness against the previous schedule; Rabe & Scheidler mine input-data patterns.

description: Planned orders or production orders per press: material, quantity, planned start and end (3-4+ weeks ahead). Moulded parts are the largest inflow of pallets into the AW.
typical_source_system: SAP PP (planned and production orders) / MES scheduling
example_fields: order_id, press_id, material, planned_qty, sched_start_ts, sched_end_ts, status, firm_flag
granularity: per order, timing to the hour
evidence: The master surgical schedule drives ward-occupancy distributions in 'An exact approach for relating recovering surgical patient workload to the master surgical schedule'. 'Temporal Fusion Transformers' treats planned values as known-future inputs.
proxy_if_missing: None needed. Ask for timestamps, not only dates.
sap_objects: PLAF (PLNUM, MATNR, GSMNG, PSTTR, PEDTR, AUFFX), AFKO (GSTRS/GSUZS scheduled start, GLTRS, GAMNG), AFPO (PSMNG, DGLTP), MDTB (MRP elements).

description: Planned punching orders on the 5 punching machines: material, quantity, start and end. These are inflows of cups and also component supply to assembly.
typical_source_system: SAP PP / MES
example_fields: order_id, machine_id, material, planned_qty, sched_start_ts, sched_end_ts
evidence: The schedule-to-occupancy logic is the same as in 'An exact approach for relating recovering surgical patient workload to the master surgical schedule'.
proxy_if_missing: None needed.
sap_objects: PLAF, AFKO, AFPO (as for moulding).

description: Assembly WOs (~3 weeks ahead, next week frozen every Wednesday): finished material, quantity, line, start and end. Each WO produces finished-goods pallets into the AW and consumes component pallboxes.
typical_source_system: SAP PP production orders; MES
example_fields: wo_id, line_id, material, qty, sched_start_ts, sched_end_ts, frozen_flag, ship_date
evidence: Known-future planned production ('Temporal Fusion Transformers'). The surgical-schedule analogue is in 'An exact approach for relating recovering surgical patient workload...'.
proxy_if_missing: None needed.
sap_objects: AFKO (GSTRS, GSUZS, GLTRS, GAMNG), AFPO (MATNR, PSMNG), RESB (components).

description: Open PO lines for purchased components and resin: material, quantity, promised delivery date (5-6 weeks ahead), quantity already received. This is the inbound plan for purchased goods.
typical_source_system: SAP MM purchasing
example_fields: po, item, schedule_line, material, plant, sched_qty, delivery_date, gr_qty, delivery_complete
evidence: 'Lead time forecasting for supplier management using machine learning' (Chalmers) and 'Supply chain data analytics for predicting supplier disruptions' both start from PO lines in the ERP.
proxy_if_missing: None needed.
sap_objects: EKKO (header), EKPO (MATNR, WERKS, MENGE, ELIKZ, LOEKZ, INSMK), EKET (EBELN, EBELP, ETENR, EINDT, MENGE, WEMNG).

data_element: Plan versions with 'as-of' timestamps (daily plan exports)
description: A full copy of every plan (assembly, moulding, punching, POs, shipments) as it looked at each extraction time, stamped with the extraction timestamp. Without plan vintages, a backtest feeds the model plans it could not have known: final-version plans make the simulator look better than it will be in production.
typical_source_system: Scheduled export job from SAP/staging DB to files or a table
example_fields: as_of_ts, plan_type, order_id, material, qty, sched_start, sched_end, status
evidence: 'Does Data Vintage Matter for Forecasting?' shows that forecasts and method rankings change when real-time vintages are used instead of final data. 'Leakage in data mining' requires timestamp-tagged learn-predict separation. 'Forecast Evaluation for Data Scientists' warns that rolling-origin evaluation is prone to leakage.
proxy_if_missing: Use Coster's offered one week of plan versions to estimate the plan-change (slip) distribution. Then apply synthetic slips to final plans in backtests and label those results as optimistic.
sap_objects: Export of PLAF/AFKO/AFPO, EKET, VBEP/LIKP with an extraction timestamp. SAP MRP list MDKP/MDTB can store a snapshot of MRP results (MDKP unverified).

description: Every AW movement with timestamps, LU id, source and destination cell, movement reason. It allows replay of occupancy at any time, measurement of cascade behaviour and estimation of dwell times.
typical_source_system: WMS (WLog, Oracle); SAP WM transfer orders / EWM warehouse tasks
example_fields: move_id, created_ts, confirmed_ts, lu_id, material, from_cell, to_cell, move_type, reason
evidence: 'A method for developing and validating simulation models for AS/RS digital twins' builds on the WMS task / WCS mission chain. 'Leakage in data mining' needs per-event timestamps for learn-predict separation.
proxy_if_missing: Difference consecutive daily snapshots (net moves per cell per day).
sap_objects: WM: LTAK (header, unverified), LTAP (VLTYP/VLPLA, NLTYP/NLPLA, VLENR/NLENR, QDATU/QZEIT, LETYP). EWM: /SCWM/ORDIM_C (confirmed), /SCWM/ORDIM_O (open).

description: Moves of pallets from the ground buffer into the AW (when space or weekly cap allows) and from the AW to the floor. These are hidden inflows into the AW that the production plan does not show.
typical_source_system: WMS (WLog) / LGV DB / manual log
example_fields: ts, lu_id, material, direction, from_loc, to_cell, reason
evidence: The Groenewout digital-twin article stresses feeding live WMS/ERP data and accurate master data into the model and validating it before use; it does not specifically discuss hidden internal transfers.
proxy_if_missing: Infer as AW putaways whose source is not a palletiser or goods-in, from the movement log.
sap_objects: LTAP (source storage type = floor), if the floor is an SAP/WMS storage type. Unverified.
check_note: Independent check: corrected. The Groenewout article discusses live WMS/ERP data feeds, master data and validation but does not mention hidden internal transfers; leanx confirms LTAP (transfer order item) with VLTYP/VLPLA/NLTYP/NLPLA/MATNR.

description: Static list of all 1,824 cells with aisle, level, side, depth, cell class (height x width), weight limit and active flag. It is needed to map LUs to compatible cells and to rebuild capacity after the August re-layout.
typical_source_system: WMS (WLog) location master; SAP bin master if SAP manages bins
example_fields: cell_id, aisle, x, level, depth, class_code, height_mm, width_mm, max_weight_kg, active, valid_from
evidence: The 'AS/RS digital twin' paper checks height type, fill state and UL type before assignment. SAP WM bins carry bin type, load capacity and total/available capacity.
proxy_if_missing: Use the class counts from the context (1,049 / 248 / 186 / 144 / 192).
sap_objects: LAGP (LGTYP, LGPLA, LPTYP bin type -> T303, LGEWI, LKAPV/RKAPV, MAXLE). EWM /SCWM/LAGP.

data_element: Load-unit type master and compatibility matrix
description: The 25 LU types with outer dimensions, gross weight and the cell classes each may use, in cascade order. This drives the 'smallest cell that fits' rule.
typical_source_system: WMS (WLog) LU-type table; SAP packaging material / storage unit type
example_fields: lu_type, length_mm, width_mm, height_mm, max_weight, allowed_classes_ordered, returnable_flag
evidence: The 'AS/RS digital twin' paper validates against UL type x starting occupancy. In SAP, storage unit types (T307) link materials (MLGN LETY1-3) to quants and transfer orders.
proxy_if_missing: Build it by hand from the 25-type list plus the cell class table.
sap_objects: T307 (storage unit type; check table of LQUA/LTAP/LEIN.LETYP), MLGN (LETY1/2/3), VEKP (VHILM, LAENG, BREIT, HOEHE), MARM (dimensions per alternative UoM).

data_element: Material -> load-unit type and quantity per load unit
description: For every material: which LU type it is packed in and how many pieces fit one LU. This converts planned quantities (pieces) into pallets per cell class, the most important conversion in the flow-balance model.
typical_source_system: SAP packing instructions / warehouse views; MES palletiser recipes
example_fields: material, lu_type, qty_per_lu, uom, valid_from
evidence: SAP keeps loading-equipment quantity per storage unit type (MLGN.LHMG1) and packing instructions (PACKKP/PACKPO). The GS1 DESADV packing structure nests products into logistic units.
proxy_if_missing: Estimate it as the median quantity per LU per material from the snapshot history.
sap_objects: MLGN (LHMG1, LETY1, LVSME), MARM (UMREZ/UMREN for a pallet-type alternative UoM), PACKKP/PACKPO (packing instruction header/item), MLGT (LPMAX, RDMNG).

description: The WMS logic: smallest compatible class first, cascade to bigger classes, exceptions per material or LU type, interaction with the allocation system. Without it, the simulator cannot route inflows to classes.
typical_source_system: WMS (WLog) configuration; documentation from Coster IT
example_fields: rule_order, lu_type, material_group, class_sequence, conditions
evidence: The 'AS/RS digital twin' paper reproduced the system's location choices exactly by coding the priority policy. SAP WM encodes this as storage type search indicators per material (MLGN.LTKZE/LTKZA).
proxy_if_missing: Infer the empirical class choice per LU type from the movement log (destination class frequencies).
sap_objects: MLGN (LTKZE putaway, LTKZA removal storage type indicator, LGBKZ storage section, BSSKZ), T305 (unverified description).

data_element: Weekly AW-entry cap per material (parameters and usage)
description: The weekly maximum of pallets per material allowed into the AW, plus the counter of how many entered each week. Pallets above the cap go to the floor buffer, so the cap splits the inflow.
typical_source_system: WMS (WLog) parameters; planner spreadsheet
example_fields: material, week, cap_pallets, entered_pallets, diverted_to_floor
evidence: In 'An exact approach for relating recovering surgical patient workload to the master surgical schedule', an upstream schedule rule (the master surgical schedule) determines downstream ward occupancy distributions; the abstract does not describe admission caps.
proxy_if_missing: Estimate caps as the weekly maximum of AW entries per material in the movement history.
sap_objects: No standard SAP object. MLGT.LPMAX (maximum bin quantity) is the nearest standard analogue and is not the same concept.
check_note: Independent check: corrected. Vanberkel et al. (JORS 62(10), 2011) derive ward occupancy distributions from a master surgical schedule but the abstract does not mention admission limits; leanx confirms MLGT.LPMAX (maximum storage bin quantity).

data_element: Unique load-unit / handling-unit ID shared across systems
description: One persistent identifier per pallet or pallbox (internal LU number or GS1 SSCC) that appears in SAP, WLog, the LGV DB and the palletiser/MES records. Without a join key, movements cannot be linked to cells, missions and orders.
typical_source_system: WMS LU number; SAP HU (EXIDV); GS1 SSCC on labels
example_fields: lu_id, sscc, sap_hu, wlog_lu, lgv_load_id, created_ts
evidence: GS1 SSCC gives a logistic unit a unique number that stays the same for its life and links it to despatch advice and EPCIS events. 'Leakage in data mining' stresses that records need proper keys and timestamps for honest analysis.
proxy_if_missing: Join on (material, qty, timestamp ±window) as a fuzzy key, accepting some mismatches.
sap_objects: VEKP.EXIDV (external HU id), VEKP.VENUM, LEIN.LENUM (WM storage unit), /SCWM/HUHDR (EWM HU header).

description: Each case where a pallet could not get a compatible cell (sent to the floor, queued, or forced into a bigger class), with time and LU type. This is the second target ('pallets that find no compatible free cell') and the ground truth for the alert.
typical_source_system: WMS (WLog) rejection or diversion log; WCS alarms
example_fields: ts, lu_id, lu_type, requested_class, outcome (floor/cascade/queue), class_fill_at_event
evidence: 'An exact approach for relating recovering surgical patient workload to the master surgical schedule' computes full ward occupancy distributions from the surgical schedule, from which the probability of exceeding capacity can be read.
proxy_if_missing: Infer from the movement log: putaways into a class bigger than the smallest compatible one, plus floor-buffer arrivals. Log these events from now on.
sap_objects: No SAP object (WMS-specific).
check_note: Independent check: corrected. Vanberkel et al. (2011) abstract computes ward occupancy distributions but does not report exceedance probabilities; no source supports the off-ward overflow claim.

data_element: Event time vs record time for every log
description: For each movement or posting, both when it physically happened and when it was recorded in the system (and the posting date). Late postings make a backtest use information that was not yet in the system at forecast time.
typical_source_system: All systems (WLog, SAP, MES, LGV)
example_fields: event_ts, recorded_ts, posting_date, source_system
evidence: GS1 EPCIS separates eventTime from recordTime ('the date and time at which this event was recorded by an EPCIS Repository'). 'Leakage in data mining' notes that databases often keep a single timestamp per record, which breaks learn-predict separation.
proxy_if_missing: Ask which timestamp each export column holds. Assume a reporting lag of up to one day for SAP postings in backtests.
sap_objects: MATDOC posting date vs entry date and time (field names unverified), AFRU.BUDAT vs ERSDA, LIKP.ERDAT/ERZET, CDHDR.UDATE/UTIME.

description: Actual goods-issue timestamps and shipped LUs (HU/SSCC) per delivery. These are the realised outflow used to measure notice-to-shipment slip and to close the flow balance.
typical_source_system: SAP SD/MM; WMS retrieval log
example_fields: delivery, actual_gi_ts, lu_id, material, qty
evidence: Little's-law space estimates need throughput at the shipping dock ('Warehouse & Distribution Science').
proxy_if_missing: Use AW retrievals with destination = shipping from the movement log.
sap_objects: LIKP.WADAT_IST, VEKP (STATUS 0050 posted for GI), MATDOC (GI postings; fields unverified).

description: Timestamp when each partially picked pallbox becomes empty and frees its cell (~130/week). This is a distinct outflow channel that no plan shows directly.
typical_source_system: WMS (WLog) / LGV DB
example_fields: lu_id, material, emptied_ts, cell_freed_ts, cell_id, cell_class
evidence: This is the length-of-stay end event in census models ('Bed census prediction combining expert opinion and patient statistics'). In SAP, a storage unit's last movement time is kept (LEIN.BDATU/BZEIT).
proxy_if_missing: Detect LUs that leave the snapshot without a shipment or a WO goods issue.
sap_objects: LEIN (BDATU/BZEIT), LQUA (quant removed), LTAP (removal TO).

data_element: Customer order book / sales schedule lines
description: Open customer orders with requested and confirmed delivery dates and quantities. The assembly plan's ship date is one input; the order book also shows orders not yet planned and the end-of-month push.
typical_source_system: SAP SD sales orders
example_fields: sales_order, item, schedule_line, material, customer, req_date, confirmed_qty, gi_date, loading_date
evidence: 'Outbound Modeling for Inventory Management' conditions warehouse drain on inventory positions and exogenous demand. Known-future demand inputs are in 'Temporal Fusion Transformers'.
proxy_if_missing: Use the assembly-plan shipping dates (available) plus month-end calendar effects.
sap_objects: VBAK/VBAP (header/item, unverified), VBEP (EDATU, WMENG, BMENG, WADAT goods-issue date, LDDAT loading date, MBDAT).

description: The planned ship date attached to each assembly WO. It links finished-goods inflow to its expected outflow (planned dwell time).
typical_source_system: SAP PP / planning sheet
example_fields: wo_id, material, qty, planned_ship_date
evidence: This is the analogue of the expected discharge date in 'Bed census prediction combining expert opinion and patient statistics': a planned leave date combined with an empirical deviation distribution.
proxy_if_missing: None needed.
sap_objects: Link via AFPO/sales order to VBEP.WADAT (unverified for Coster's setup).

description: Delivery documents created when a shipment is notified (FCA ~48 h, DAP ~24 h, affiliate containers 48-72 h before): creation timestamp, planned goods-issue date, incoterm, package count. This is the most reliable 1-3 day outflow signal.
typical_source_system: SAP SD deliveries; TMS / carrier booking; email notices
example_fields: delivery, created_ts, planned_gi_date, actual_gi_date, incoterm, n_packages, ship_to, route
evidence: Short-notice discharges are the hospital analogue in 'Bed census prediction combining expert opinion and patient statistics'. SAP LIKP keeps both creation time and planned and actual goods-movement dates, so lead time from notice to goods issue can be measured.
proxy_if_missing: Model outbound as assembly-plan ship dates shifted by the incoterm-specific notice lead time.
sap_objects: LIKP (ERDAT/ERZET, WADAT, WADAT_IST, LFDAT/LFUHR, LDDAT, INCO1, ANZPK, KUNNR), LIPS (LFIMG, VGBEL), VEKP/VEPO (HUs per delivery). Shipment header VTTK unverified.

description: Date and quantity of each component needed by each assembly WO. Converted to pallboxes, this is the retrieval demand on the AW and the source of partial-pallbox returns.
typical_source_system: SAP PP reservations / dependent requirements
example_fields: reservation, item, wo_id, component, req_date, req_qty, withdrawn_qty, final_issue_flag
evidence: 'ISA-95 Common Object Model (OPC 10030)' links material definitions to the operations that consume them. 'Input data management in simulation' lists production orders and material requirements as core simulation inputs.
proxy_if_missing: Compute it as WO quantity x BOM quantity per component.
sap_objects: RESB (RSNUM, RSPOS, MATNR, BDTER, BDMNG, ENMNG, AUFNR, KZEAR), MDTB (dependent requirements).

description: One row per AW cell at the snapshot time: occupied or free, which load unit, material and quantity. This is the starting state for the flow-balance simulator and the source of the target series.
typical_source_system: WMS (WLog, Oracle); mirrored in SAP WM/EWM bin and quant tables if SAP manages bins
example_fields: snapshot_ts, cell_id, aisle, level, cell_class, occupied_flag, lu_id, lu_type, material, qty, gr_date
evidence: Starting occupancy is a design factor in 'A method for developing and validating simulation models for AS/RS digital twins'. 'Warehouse & Distribution Science' estimates space from position censuses plus Little's law.
proxy_if_missing: None. This is the core asset. If cell-level rows are missing, use class-level counts and lose the cascade logic.
sap_objects: WM: LAGP (bin: LPTYP, KZLER, KZVOL), LQUA (quant: LGPLA, LENUM, WDATU, BESTQ). EWM: /SCWM/LAGP, /SCWM/QUAN, /SCWM/AQUA. Coster's bins are in WLog, so SAP may hold only storage-location totals (MARD).

data_element: Daily occupancy per cell class since the August 2026 layout change
description: Occupied, free and blocked cells per class (Low, Medium, High, Medium W1000, High W1000) for every day since the re-layout. This is the target time series for the backtest.
typical_source_system: Derived from WMS snapshots (WLog)
example_fields: date, cell_class, n_cells_total, n_occupied, n_free, n_blocked, fill_ratio
evidence: Bed-census papers such as 'Can we accurately forecast non-elective bed occupancy...' and 'Bed census prediction combining expert opinion and patient statistics' forecast the aggregate census per ward, which is the analogue of a cell class.
proxy_if_missing: Rebuild from archived 06:00 snapshot files if they exist. Otherwise start logging now and backfill with the movement log.
sap_objects: Aggregate of LAGP/LQUA or /SCWM/LAGP by bin type (LPTYP). WLog is the system of record.

description: Number and identity of pallets on the ~800-slot floor buffer per day: material, LU type, and why each is there (weekly cap, no compatible cell, QC). Overflow to the floor is the real symptom of AW saturation, and floor pallets come back into the AW when space frees.
typical_source_system: WMS (WLog) if floor slots are virtual bins; otherwise SAP storage location or a spreadsheet
example_fields: date, floor_slot, lu_id, material, lu_type, reason_code, arrival_ts, planned_putaway_ts
evidence: 'Warehouse & Distribution Science' (Bartholdi & Hackman) compares dedicated and shared storage: shared storage uses space better but complicates put-away and picking.
proxy_if_missing: Count floor pallets daily by a manual tally or photo; or infer them as AW-bound inflows that do not appear in the AW snapshot.
sap_objects: If floor slots are SAP bins: LAGP/LQUA for a separate storage type (LGTYP). Otherwise only MARD by storage location. Unverified for Coster.
check_note: Independent check: corrected. Bartholdi & Hackman's book compares dedicated and shared storage (no overflow discussion found in the visible text); the Groenewout article does not mention hidden overflow areas. LAGP/LQUA/MARD are standard SAP tables.

data_element: Cell status: blocked, reserved, out of service (with history)
description: Which cells are unusable or held on each day and why (maintenance, damage, putaway or removal block, reserved by the allocation system). Only 1,819 of 1,824 cells are in use, and blocked cells shrink the real capacity of a class.
typical_source_system: WMS (WLog) cell table; SAP WM/EWM bin blocks
example_fields: date, cell_id, status (free/occupied/blocked_in/blocked_out/reserved/disabled), block_reason, valid_from, valid_to
evidence: SAP WM keeps separate user and system putaway/removal blocks plus a blocking reason per bin (LAGP SKZUE/SKZUA/SPGRU). 'A method for developing and validating simulation models for AS/RS digital twins' checks the fill state of each location before assignment.
proxy_if_missing: Use the static cell master with the counts in use. Treat the gap between total cells and (occupied + free) in each snapshot as blocked.
sap_objects: LAGP: SKZUE, SKZUA, SKZSE, SKZSA, SPGRU (reason, check table T330), KZLER (empty), KZVOL (full), ANZLE/MAXLE (SU count). EWM: /SCWM/LAGP.

data_element: Allocation-system reservations and hold-back of wide cells
description: How many W1000 cells the 'allocation system' keeps back, for which LU types, and when it releases them. On 20 May 2026, 110 wide cells stayed free while 800-mm Medium was 100% full, so the real per-class capacity differs from the nominal one.
typical_source_system: WMS (WLog) allocation parameters; possibly the WCS
example_fields: rule_id, cell_class, reserved_count_or_pct, eligible_lu_types, release_condition, valid_from
evidence: The 'AS/RS digital twin' paper (Ferrari et al. 2023) reached a 0.49% median error after iterative calibration of timing parameters, and its model chose the same storage locations as the physical system in every trial.
proxy_if_missing: Infer from snapshots: the free cells per class that persist on days when the smaller classes are full give the effective reserve.
sap_objects: No standard SAP object. In SAP WM a comparable logic lives in storage type search and bin-type search strategies (unverified for Coster).
check_note: Independent check: corrected. Ferrari et al. (IJAMT 2023) report a 0.49% median error and matching storage locations in all trials, but attribute accuracy gains to timing/stochastic calibration, not to modelling the storage-assignment policy.

data_element: Load-unit away-from-cell status (at picking, in transit)
description: Pallboxes that are out at an assembly machine, on an LGV or on a conveyor. You need to know whether their AW cell stays reserved while they are away, because a partial pallbox frees its cell only when it is empty.
typical_source_system: WMS (WLog) LU status; LGV DB (SQL Server)
example_fields: lu_id, status (in_cell/out_for_picking/in_transit/on_floor), home_cell_id, cell_reserved_flag, status_ts
evidence: SAP WM storage units carry a status (in bin, in removal, in putaway, in posting change) in LEIN.STATU. The 'AS/RS digital twin' paper separates WMS tasks from WCS missions for the same reason.
proxy_if_missing: Ask for the picking rule in words (cell kept or released while out). Model the expected count of LUs out from the LGV picking-mission rate times the average away time.
sap_objects: LEIN (STATU, BDATU/BZEIT). EWM: /SCWM/ORDIM_O (open warehouse tasks).

data_element: Age of stock / goods-receipt date per load unit
description: Date and time each LU entered the AW, so that time in storage so far can be computed for every occupied cell. Needed for dwell-time (length-of-stay) distributions and for FIFO-driven retrieval timing.
typical_source_system: WMS (WLog) LU record; SAP WM quant GR date
example_fields: lu_id, putaway_ts, gr_date, last_movement_ts
evidence: 'Duration-of-Stay Storage Assignment under Uncertainty' predicts pallet duration of stay from date of arrival, product group and customer type (8.44 M pallets). 'Bed census prediction combining expert opinion and patient statistics' combines elapsed stay with LoS distributions.
proxy_if_missing: Track each LU id across consecutive daily snapshots to get first-seen and last-seen dates (day resolution).
sap_objects: LQUA.WDATU (GR date), LQUA.BDATU (last movement), LEIN.BDATU/BZEIT.

description: Days to month or quarter end, customer-specific shipping days, and container sailing or pickup schedules. These explain the end-of-month finished-goods build-up and shipment waves.
typical_source_system: Derived from the calendar; SD shipping calendar; TMS
example_fields: date, days_to_month_end, is_month_end_week, customer_ship_day_flags
evidence: Calendar effects as known-future inputs ('Temporal Fusion Transformers'). In 'Can we accurately forecast non-elective bed occupancy...', holiday-day variables (with temperature and precipitation) improved forecast accuracy.
proxy_if_missing: Derive from dates. Get customer ship days from the history of outbound goods-issue timestamps.
sap_objects: TFACS for workdays. Route/shipping calendars in SD are unverified.
check_note: Independent check: corrected. TFT abstract confirms known-future inputs; the BMJ Open MSARIMA paper reports holiday days, temperature and precipitation improved forecasts (holiday-day variables, not holiday-week dummies); leanx confirms TFACS as the factory calendar table.

description: A timestamped event each time a palletiser completes a pallet (line, material, quantity, LU id). This is the finest inflow signal and it leads the AW putaway by the conveyor and LGV transit time.
typical_source_system: MES (SQL Server); palletiser PLC
example_fields: event_ts, line_id, lu_id, material, qty, lu_type
evidence: 'State of the Art and Future Directions of Digital Twins for Production Logistics' recommends the MES as the central data hub for historical and real-time data.
proxy_if_missing: Use WMS putaway timestamps minus a typical transit time.
sap_objects: No SAP object (MES). It may surface as goods receipts (MATDOC) if back-flushed per pallet.

data_element: Supplier order confirmations and inbound ASN (DESADV)
description: Supplier-confirmed dates and quantities, and despatch advices sent before the truck leaves (pallet count, SSCCs, contents). They sharpen the 1-3 day inbound forecast far beyond the PO date.
typical_source_system: SAP MM vendor confirmations / inbound deliveries; EDI (EANCOM DESADV); supplier portal
example_fields: po, item, conf_category, conf_date, conf_time, conf_qty, inbound_delivery, n_pallets, sscc_list, created_ts
evidence: GS1 EANCOM DESADV is sent before the goods move so the receiver can plan receipt, and it carries SSCC-identified logistic units. In the Chalmers lead-time thesis, the supplier's own estimates reached only 0.343 binned accuracy against 0.804 for the ML model.
proxy_if_missing: Use PO dates plus an empirical supplier slip distribution. Ask goods-in for truck pre-notifications (emails, phone calls) as a manual log.
sap_objects: EKES (EBTYP confirmation category, EINDT, UZEIT, MENGE, VBELN inbound delivery, ERDAT), LIKP/LIPS for inbound deliveries, VEKP/VEPO for HUs.

description: Coster's internal estimate of pallets arriving per day (file 4). Useful as a benchmark and as a covariate. Its timing (when it was made) must be stored.
typical_source_system: Planner spreadsheet / staging DB
example_fields: forecast_made_ts, target_date, n_pallets_expected, material_group
evidence: In 'Bed census prediction combining expert opinion and patient statistics', combining expert estimates (expected discharge dates) with data-driven distributions gave precise census predictions.
proxy_if_missing: Use PO schedule lines plus production plans converted to pallets.
sap_objects: Not a standard SAP object (likely Excel/staging).

data_element: Historical plan reconstruction via SAP change documents
description: SAP writes change documents (old value, new value, user, date, time) for many business objects. Where it does so for PO schedule lines or orders, past delivery dates and quantities can be rebuilt as of any date, which partly replaces the missing plan history.
typical_source_system: SAP Basis change-document tables
example_fields: objectclas, objectid, changenr, udate, utime, tabname, fname, value_old, value_new
evidence: 'Does Data Vintage Matter for Forecasting?' argues for evaluating on vintages. Change documents are the ERP's built-in vintage record. 'Leakage in data mining' notes that databases often lose time-of-knowledge information.
proxy_if_missing: If change documents are not active for these objects, start daily plan exports now. Meanwhile approximate plan changes from the one week of plan versions Coster offers.
sap_objects: CDHDR (OBJECTCLAS, OBJECTID, CHANGENR, UDATE, UTIME, TCODE), CDPOS (TABNAME, FNAME, VALUE_OLD, VALUE_NEW). Object classes for POs (EINKBELEG) and production orders are unverified; check coverage at Coster.

description: Which plan items are frozen or firmed (assembly week frozen every Wednesday, firmed planned orders) and the planning time fence. Frozen items slip less, so Monte Carlo slip distributions should depend on this flag.
typical_source_system: SAP PP/MRP; planning procedure
example_fields: order_id, firm_flag, frozen_since_ts, time_fence_days
evidence: 'New lot-sizing formulations for less nervous production schedules' defines nervousness as changes between successive rolling plans and cites evidence that freezing the schedule improves stability.
proxy_if_missing: Derive the flag from the rule (orders in the next week after Wednesday = frozen).
sap_objects: PLAF.AUFFX (firming indicator), MARC.FXHOR (planning time fence).

data_element: Defrag rule parameters and defrag missions
description: Saturation threshold, idle windows and the per-mission log (25-80 moves per week) that move small pallets from big cells back into small cells. They change the per-class occupancy without any inflow or outflow.
typical_source_system: WMS (WLog) / WCS
example_fields: mission_id, ts, lu_id, from_cell, from_class, to_cell, to_class, trigger_threshold
evidence: Relocation moves are part of the WMS task stream that 'A method for developing and validating simulation models for AS/RS digital twins' turns into crane missions.
proxy_if_missing: Model defrag as a weekly transfer between classes, sized from the snapshot-to-snapshot class shifts with no net inflow.
sap_objects: WM: LTAP (VLTYP/VLPLA -> NLTYP/NLPLA, QDATU/QZEIT). EWM: /SCWM/ORDIM_C.

description: Missions of the 5 LGVs: type (supply to machine, return partial, putaway from palletiser, floor transfer), create, start and end times, LU id, from and to. It shows LUs out of cells and transport bottlenecks.
typical_source_system: LGV fleet management DB (SQL Server)
example_fields: mission_id, type, lu_id, from_loc, to_loc, created_ts, start_ts, end_ts, status
evidence: WCS missions are explicit model inputs in 'A method for developing and validating simulation models for AS/RS digital twins'. 'From a simulation model to a digital twin' warns that small timing errors compound.
proxy_if_missing: Use WMS retrieval and return timestamps for the same LU.
sap_objects: No SAP object (LGV DB).

description: Material type (resin, cup, valve, actuator, packaging), procurement type (in-house or purchased), MRP controller, product family, ABC/turnover class. They let you model and evaluate errors by segment and pool data across similar materials.
typical_source_system: SAP material master (MARA/MARC)
example_fields: material, material_type, procurement_type, mrp_controller, product_family, abc_class, planned_delivery_days
evidence: In 'Duration-of-Stay Storage Assignment', product group and customer type were the key features. In the Chalmers lead-time thesis, ABC class, purchase group and country were selected features.
proxy_if_missing: Derive families from material-code prefixes and turnover classes from the movement log.
sap_objects: MARC (BESKZ procurement type, DISPO, PLIFZ, WEBAZ, DZEIT, EISBE), MARA (material type, unverified field list).

data_element: Manual consolidation and manual operations log
description: Dates and scope of manual consolidations (every 3-4 months), manual relocations, emergency clear-outs and overrides. They cause step changes in occupancy that a model would otherwise treat as noise.
typical_source_system: Paper or spreadsheet logs; WMS manual-transaction flag
example_fields: date, operation_type, n_lu_moved, classes_affected, operator, notes
evidence: 'Data quality problems in discrete event simulation...' names limited accessibility and data not designed for simulation as core problems. Undocumented manual work is the typical gap.
proxy_if_missing: Flag days with large class shifts and no matching plan movements. Ask the warehouse lead to reconstruct the dates of recent consolidations.
sap_objects: If manual moves are WMS transfer orders: LTAP with a manual movement type (unverified).

data_element: Machine downtime and MES machine states
description: Stops of presses, punching machines and assembly lines (planned maintenance, breakdowns, mould changes). They make actual inflow and consumption deviate from plan and are what-if levers ('stop a press').
typical_source_system: MES (SQL Server); maintenance system (SAP PM)
example_fields: machine_id, state, start_ts, end_ts, reason_code
evidence: 'Data quality problems in discrete event simulation...' reports a lack of data on minor stoppages. 'Modeling for Non-Exponential Production Systems Using Parts Flow Data' notes the low quality of operating-status data and estimates downtime from part counts instead.
proxy_if_missing: Use the gap between planned and confirmed output per order as an aggregate downtime proxy.
sap_objects: AFRU (actual execution times). SAP PM notification and order tables unverified.

description: Actual component withdrawals per assembly WO with timestamps. Together with the reservation they show how fast pallboxes empty.
typical_source_system: SAP MM material documents; MES consumption; back-flush
example_fields: wo_id, component, qty, gi_ts, lu_id
evidence: Part-flow based estimation in 'Modeling for Non-Exponential Production Systems Using Parts Flow Data'.
proxy_if_missing: Use LGV picking missions (LU out and back) and the emptied-pallbox log.
sap_objects: RESB.ENMNG, MATDOC (GI to order; fields unverified), AFRU (back-flush via confirmation).

description: Rules for container shipments to affiliate plants (70 pallboxes each, 48-72 h notice) and any other batch dispatches. One container removes 70 LUs in a block, which matters for the per-class free-cell forecast.
typical_source_system: Logistics planning rules
example_fields: rule, lu_per_container, notice_hours, typical_days, lu_types
evidence: 'Flexible nurse staffing based on hourly bed census predictions' predicts hourly bed census from variable patient arrivals and lengths of stay; it does not address batch discharges.
proxy_if_missing: Treat each announced container as an outflow block of 70 LUs of the planned material.
sap_objects: LIKP/VEKP per container delivery.
check_note: Independent check: corrected. Kortbeek et al. (IJPE 161, 2015) abstract attributes census variability to arrivals and lengths of stay and does not discuss batch discharges; leanx confirms LIKP (delivery header) and VEKP (handling unit header, linked to deliveries via VPOBJKEY).

description: Occupancy per class several times a day. Palletiser waves and LGV picking cycles can peak between two 06:00 snapshots, and an alert '40-48 h ahead' needs to know when within the day saturation occurs.
typical_source_system: WMS (WLog) current-state table, logged by a scheduled job; or reconstructed from the movement log
example_fields: ts, cell_class, n_occupied, n_free, n_in_transit
evidence: 'Flexible nurse staffing based on hourly bed census predictions' shows the value of hourly census over daily census for capacity decisions.
proxy_if_missing: Replay the WMS movement log (file 3) from the 06:00 state to rebuild hourly occupancy. Or add a cron job on the staging DB that copies the class counts every hour from now on.
sap_objects: No standard SAP object (WLog-specific). EWM: /SCWM/LAGP and /SCWM/QUAN are current-state only.

data_element: Quality / quarantine status per load unit
description: Stock category of each LU (unrestricted, in QC, blocked, returns). Quarantined pallets occupy cells but cannot be shipped or consumed, so they stay longer and distort dwell-time estimates.
typical_source_system: SAP QM (inspection lots); WMS stock category
example_fields: lu_id, material, batch, stock_category, inspection_lot, lot_created, usage_decision_date
evidence: SAP WM quants carry BESTQ (Q=quality, S=blocked, R=returns). In 'ISA-95 Common Object Model (OPC 10030)', status and test results are attached to the material lot.
proxy_if_missing: Add the stock-category column to the daily snapshot export. Otherwise use QALS lots with no usage decision as the quarantine set.
sap_objects: LQUA.BESTQ, LTAP.BESTQ, MARD.INSME/SPEME, QALS (PRUEFLOS, ART, ENSTEHDAT, PAENDTERM, STAT35 usage decision), EKPO/MARC.INSMK.

data_element: Empty returnable containers in the AW
description: Count and location of the ~300 metal containers that return empty and still take a cell. Also their expected return and outbound schedule. This is a non-production inflow that the production plan does not show.
typical_source_system: WMS (WLog) with LU type = empty container; container pool spreadsheet
example_fields: date, lu_type, n_empty_in_aw, n_empty_on_floor, expected_returns, expected_dispatch
evidence: SAP handling units distinguish packaging materials (VEKP.VHILM/VHART), so empties are traceable as HU types. 'From a simulation model to a digital twin' warns that incomplete master data causes model drift.
proxy_if_missing: Filter the snapshot for LU types with no material or zero quantity. Use a constant or a weekly profile if the return schedule is not available.
sap_objects: VEKP (VHILM, VHART, STATUS), VEPO (VELIN=2 auxiliary packaging). Returnable packaging accounts in SAP are unverified for Coster.

description: Remaining quantity in each partially picked pallbox compared with a full one. It tells when a pallbox will empty and free its cell (~130 per week).
typical_source_system: WMS (WLog) LU quantity; MES consumption
example_fields: lu_id, material, qty_remaining, qty_full, last_pick_ts
evidence: SAP WM quants hold total, available and to-remove quantities (LQUA GESME/VERME/AUSME). Hospital census models use expected discharge per occupant ('Bed census prediction...').
proxy_if_missing: qty_remaining = qty in snapshot. Estimate emptying time from the BOM consumption rate of the assembly WO that uses it.
sap_objects: LQUA (GESME, VERME, AUSME), packaging spec PACKPO for full quantity.

description: Forecasts or call-off schedules received from major customers and affiliates (EDI or email). They extend outflow visibility beyond firm orders for the 7-14 day horizon.
typical_source_system: SAP SD (scheduling agreements) / EDI / email
example_fields: customer, material, period, forecast_qty, received_ts
evidence: Exogenous demand is a conditioning input in 'Outbound Modeling for Inventory Management'. The TFT input taxonomy ('Temporal Fusion Transformers') treats such forecasts as known future values.
proxy_if_missing: Use the assembly-plan shipping dates and the order book.
sap_objects: Scheduling agreement schedule lines (VBEP for SD documents). EDI forecast message types unverified.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. arXiv 2507.10890 models outbound drain conditioned on exogenous customer demand; TFT treats known future inputs separately; leanx confirms VBEP as sales document schedule lines (EDATU, WMENG).

description: Supplier capacity notices, holidays at supplier sites, and transport disruptions (strikes, Brenner pass closures). Rarely decisive at 48 h, but they explain clustered inbound slips.
typical_source_system: Supplier communication; public sources
example_fields: date, supplier, event_type, expected_delay_days
evidence: An appliedAI inbound-logistics case combined supplier data with public indicators to estimate inbound volumes and reported ~20% better warehouse utilisation. The 'supplier disruptions' paper used engineered features from historical OEM data.
proxy_if_missing: Ignore initially. Add supplier holiday calendars for the top suppliers.
sap_objects: None.
check_note: Independent check: confirmed. appliedAI page confirms combining supplier data with public indicators and ~20% better warehouse utilisation; Brintrup et al. (IJPR 58(11), 2020) predict supplier disruptions from engineered OEM data features.

description: Low-level crane missions with times. Needed only if crane throughput or queueing limits how fast cells free or fill (e.g., during defrag or peaks).
typical_source_system: WCS / PLC logs
example_fields: mission_id, crane_id, type, from_cell, to_cell, start_ts, end_ts
evidence: The 'AS/RS digital twin' paper shows that deterministic travel times underestimated storage time by about 4-12% and that stochastic timings were required.
proxy_if_missing: Ignore for daily occupancy. Use WMS move timestamps if throughput matters.
sap_objects: No SAP object.

description: Scrap and rework per order and component scrap allowances. They change pallet counts versus plan, and rework pallets may sit in the AW longer.
typical_source_system: SAP PP confirmations; MES quality
example_fields: order_id, scrap_qty, rework_qty, reason
evidence: Production confirmations carry yield, scrap and rework separately (SAP AFRU). Bills of materials carry component scrap % (STPO.AUSCH).
proxy_if_missing: Apply the average yield ratio per department.
sap_objects: AFRU (LMNGA, XMNGA, RMNGA), STPO.AUSCH.

description: Downtime of stacker cranes, conveyors and LGVs. During an outage, inflows queue on conveyors or go to the floor, and retrievals stop.
typical_source_system: WCS / LGV DB alarms; maintenance log
example_fields: equipment_id, start_ts, end_ts, type, impact
evidence: 'From a simulation model to a digital twin' lists maintenance systems as inputs for a live twin.
proxy_if_missing: Detect gaps in movement timestamps longer than X minutes during working shifts.
sap_objects: SAP PM (unverified).

data_element: Inventory record discrepancies and cycle-count corrections
description: Differences between WMS records and physical reality (ghost pallets, unrecorded moves) and the correction postings. They indicate how reliable the snapshot target itself is.
typical_source_system: WMS inventory/count transactions; SAP physical inventory
example_fields: count_date, cell_id, recorded_lu, found_lu, correction_type
evidence: 'Inventory Record Inaccuracy: An Empirical Analysis' found 65% of ~370,000 retail inventory records inaccurate. Auditing reduced and complexity increased the inaccuracy.
proxy_if_missing: Compare snapshot LU ids with the movement log. LUs appearing or disappearing without a movement are record errors.
sap_objects: Physical inventory documents and MATDOC adjustment postings (unverified).

description: Booked truck and container pickup slots and inbound truck slots. They tie shipment notices to actual departure times and show daily outbound capacity.
typical_source_system: TMS / carrier portal / dock planning spreadsheet
example_fields: slot_ts, direction, carrier, n_pallets_planned, delivery_ref
evidence: 'From a simulation model to a digital twin' lists transport and dock planning systems as live inputs for a warehouse twin.
proxy_if_missing: Use LIKP planned goods-issue and loading dates.
sap_objects: LIKP (LDDAT, TDDAT). Shipment tables (VTTK/VTTP) unverified.
